01-01.text: The Emancipation Proclamation takes effect, declaring enslaved people in Confederate states free.

01-02.text: Georgia ratifies the US Constitution, becoming the fourth state.

01-04.text: Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, falls back to Earth after three months in orbit.

01-05.text: Henry Ford announces the $5 workday, doubling many workers' pay.

01-06.text: FDR gives his Four Freedoms speech to Congress.

01-07.text: The first commercial transatlantic phone call connects New York and London.

01-08.text: Andrew Jackson wins the Battle of New Orleans.

01-09.text: Steve Jobs unveils the first iPhone.

01-10.text: The League of Nations is founded.

01-11.text: Insulin is first given to a diabetic patient, a 14-year-old boy in Toronto.

01-12.text: Hattie Caraway becomes the first woman elected to the US Senate.

01-13.text: Emile Zola publishes J'accuse, defending Alfred Dreyfus.

01-14.text: Congress ratifies the Treaty of Paris, ending the Revolutionary War.

01-15.text: The British Museum opens to the public in London.

01-16.text: The 18th Amendment is ratified, bringing Prohibition.

01-17.text: Captain Cook's ships become the first known to cross the Antarctic Circle.

01-18.text: Captain James Cook becomes the first known European to reach Hawaii.

01-19.text: Indira Gandhi is chosen to lead India, its first woman prime minister.

01-20.text: John F. Kennedy is sworn in: "Ask not what your country can do for you."

01-21.text: King Louis XVI of France is executed in Paris.

01-22.text: Queen Victoria dies after reigning nearly 64 years.

01-23.text: Elizabeth Blackwell becomes the first woman to earn a medical degree in the US.

01-24.text: Gold is found at Sutter's Mill, starting the California Gold Rush.

01-25.text: Reporter Nellie Bly finishes her trip around the world in 72 days.

01-26.text: The First Fleet lands at Sydney Cove, now marked as Australia Day.

01-27.text: Thomas Edison is granted his patent for the electric lamp.

01-28.text: Space Shuttle Challenger breaks apart after launch, lost with its crew of seven.

01-29.text: Karl Benz files the patent for his Motorwagen, the first true automobile.

01-30.text: The Beatles play their last public show, on a London rooftop.

01-31.text: Explorer 1, America's first satellite, is launched.

02-01.text: Four Black students sit in at a Greensboro lunch counter, sparking sit-ins nationwide.

02-02.text: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo ends the Mexican-American War.

02-03.text: Buddy Holly dies in a plane crash: The Day the Music Died.

02-04.text: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin meet at the Yalta Conference.

02-05.text: Chaplin, Pickford, Fairbanks and Griffith found United Artists.

02-06.text: Elizabeth II becomes Queen at age 25.

02-07.text: The Beatles land in New York for their first US visit.

02-08.text: The Boy Scouts of America is incorporated.

02-09.text: The Beatles play The Ed Sullivan Show for about 73 million viewers.

02-10.text: The Treaty of Paris ends the Seven Years' War.

02-11.text: Nelson Mandela walks free after 27 years in prison.

02-12.text: Abraham Lincoln and Charles Darwin are born on the same day.

02-13.text: France tests its first atomic bomb in the Sahara.

02-14.text: Alexander Graham Bell files his telephone patent.

02-15.text: The USS Maine explodes in Havana harbor.

02-16.text: Howard Carter opens the sealed burial chamber of King Tut.

02-17.text: The House breaks the Jefferson-Burr tie, making Thomas Jefferson president.

02-19.text: US Marines land on Iwo Jima.

02-20.text: John Glenn becomes the first American to orbit Earth.

02-22.text: George Washington is born in Virginia.

02-23.text: Marines raise the US flag on Iwo Jima's Mount Suribachi.

02-24.text: Pope Gregory XIII issues the decree creating the Gregorian calendar.

02-26.text: Grand Canyon National Park is established.

02-27.text: The Reichstag, Germany's parliament building, is set on fire.

02-28.text: Watson and Crick work out the double-helix structure of DNA.

02-29.text: Hattie McDaniel becomes the first Black actor to win an Oscar.

03-01.text: Yellowstone becomes the world's first national park.

03-03.text: The Star-Spangled Banner becomes the US national anthem.

03-04.text: FDR is sworn in: "The only thing we have to fear is fear itself."

03-06.text: The Alamo falls after a 13-day siege.

03-07.text: Alexander Graham Bell is granted the telephone patent.

03-08.text: Women's marches in Petrograd help spark the Russian Revolution.

03-09.text: Barbie debuts at the American Toy Fair in New York.

03-10.text: Bell makes the first phone call: "Mr. Watson, come here."

03-11.text: The Great Blizzard of 1888 begins, burying the US Northeast.

03-12.text: Juliette Gordon Low founds the Girl Scouts in Savannah.

03-13.text: William Herschel discovers the planet Uranus.

03-14.text: Albert Einstein is born in Ulm, Germany.

03-15.text: Julius Caesar is assassinated in Rome on the Ides of March.

03-16.text: Robert Goddard launches the first liquid-fueled rocket.

03-17.text: New York holds its first St. Patrick's Day parade.

03-18.text: Alexei Leonov makes the first spacewalk.

03-19.text: Congress sets US time zones and daylight saving time.

03-20.text: Uncle Tom's Cabin is published as a book.

03-22.text: Britain passes the Stamp Act, angering the American colonies.

03-23.text: Patrick Henry declares, "Give me liberty, or give me death!"

03-24.text: Robert Koch announces he has found the germ that causes tuberculosis.

03-25.text: The Treaty of Rome is signed, founding the European Economic Community.

03-26.text: Jonas Salk announces his polio vaccine.

03-27.text: The Good Friday earthquake, magnitude 9.2, strikes Alaska.

03-28.text: An accident at Three Mile Island partly melts a reactor core.

03-29.text: The last US combat troops leave Vietnam.

03-30.text: The US agrees to buy Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million.

03-31.text: The Eiffel Tower is inaugurated in Paris.

04-01.text: Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak found Apple.

04-02.text: Ponce de Leon sights Florida and claims it for Spain.

04-03.text: The Pony Express makes its first run.

04-05.text: Pocahontas marries John Rolfe in Jamestown.

04-06.text: The first modern Olympic Games open in Athens.

04-07.text: The World Health Organization is founded.

04-08.text: Hank Aaron hits home run 715, passing Babe Ruth.

04-09.text: Robert E. Lee surrenders at Appomattox Court House.

04-10.text: The Titanic sails from Southampton on its maiden voyage.

04-12.text: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space.

04-13.text: Thomas Jefferson is born in Virginia.

04-14.text: Noah Webster publishes his American Dictionary of the English Language.

04-15.text: The Titanic sinks after hitting an iceberg.

04-16.text: Harriet Quimby becomes the first woman to fly across the English Channel.

04-17.text: Giovanni da Verrazzano sails into New York Harbor.

04-18.text: Paul Revere rides to warn that the British are coming.

04-19.text: The Battles of Lexington and Concord begin the American Revolution.

04-20.text: Jacques Cartier sets sail on the voyage that reaches Canada.

04-21.text: Rome is founded, according to legend, by Romulus.

04-22.text: The first Earth Day is celebrated.

04-23.text: William Shakespeare is born (traditional date) in Stratford-upon-Avon.

04-24.text: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched.

04-25.text: Work begins on the Suez Canal.

04-26.text: The Jamestown settlers first land in Virginia, at Cape Henry.

04-27.text: Explorer Ferdinand Magellan is killed in the Philippines.

04-28.text: Mutiny on the Bounty: Fletcher Christian seizes the ship.

04-29.text: Prince William marries Catherine Middleton at Westminster Abbey.

04-30.text: The Louisiana Purchase is signed, doubling the size of the US.

05-02.text: The Hudson's Bay Company is chartered.

05-03.text: Gone with the Wind wins the Pulitzer Prize.

05-04.text: Peter Minuit arrives in New Netherland; he soon buys Manhattan.

05-05.text: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space.

05-06.text: Roger Bannister runs the first four-minute mile.

05-07.text: Germany signs its unconditional surrender at Reims, France.

05-08.text: V-E Day: World War II ends in Europe.

05-09.text: The FDA approves the first birth control pill.

05-10.text: The golden spike completes the first transcontinental railroad.

05-11.text: IBM's Deep Blue beats chess champion Garry Kasparov.

05-12.text: Florence Nightingale is born in Florence, Italy.

05-13.text: The US declares war on Mexico.

05-14.text: Jamestown, the first lasting English colony in America, is founded.

05-15.text: The McDonald brothers open their first restaurant in California.

05-16.text: The first Academy Awards are held in Hollywood.

05-17.text: Brown v. Board of Education ends legal school segregation.

05-18.text: Mount St. Helens erupts in Washington State.

05-19.text: New England's Dark Day: the sky goes black at midday.

05-20.text: Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis patent riveted blue jeans.

05-21.text: Charles Lindbergh lands in Paris after the first solo nonstop Atlantic flight.

05-22.text: The Wright brothers are granted their airplane patent.

05-23.text: The New York Public Library's main building is dedicated.

05-27.text: The Golden Gate Bridge opens to pedestrians.

05-28.text: The Dionne quintuplets are born in Ontario.

05-29.text: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reach the top of Everest.

05-31.text: Big Ben's clock starts keeping time in London.

06-01.text: CNN, the first 24-hour news channel, goes on the air.

06-02.text: Queen Elizabeth II is crowned at Westminster Abbey.

06-03.text: Ed White makes the first American spacewalk.

06-04.text: The Montgolfier brothers fly a hot-air balloon in public for the first time.

06-05.text: George Marshall proposes the Marshall Plan to rebuild Europe.

06-06.text: D-Day: Allied troops land on the beaches of Normandy.

06-07.text: Richard Henry Lee moves that the colonies declare independence.

06-08.text: George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four is published.

06-09.text: Secretariat wins the Belmont by 31 lengths to take the Triple Crown.

06-10.text: Alcoholics Anonymous is founded in Akron, Ohio.

06-11.text: Congress picks five men, including Jefferson, to draft the Declaration.

06-12.text: Reagan in Berlin: "Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall!"

06-13.text: Miranda v. Arizona: police must read suspects their rights.

06-14.text: Congress adopts the Stars and Stripes as the US flag.

06-15.text: King John seals the Magna Carta at Runnymede.

06-16.text: Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman in space.

06-17.text: The Statue of Liberty arrives in New York Harbor, in 350 pieces.

06-19.text: Juneteenth: enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, learn they are free.

06-21.text: New Hampshire ratifies the Constitution, putting it into effect.

06-22.text: Galileo is forced to recant his view that Earth circles the Sun.

06-24.text: John Cabot lands in North America.

06-25.text: Custer's Last Stand at the Little Bighorn.

06-26.text: The United Nations Charter is signed in San Francisco.

06-27.text: Helen Keller is born in Tuscumbia, Alabama.

06-28.text: The Treaty of Versailles is signed, formally ending World War I.

06-29.text: The Globe Theatre burns down during a show of Shakespeare's Henry VIII.

06-30.text: The Tunguska blast flattens 800 square miles of Siberian forest.

07-01.text: Canada becomes a country through Confederation.

07-02.text: Amelia Earhart vanishes over the Pacific.

07-04.text: Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence.

07-05.text: Dolly the sheep, the first cloned mammal, is born.

07-06.text: Louis Pasteur first uses his rabies vaccine, saving a boy.

07-07.text: Construction begins on the Hoover Dam.

07-08.text: The Wall Street Journal is first published.

07-09.text: The first Wimbledon tennis championship begins.

07-10.text: The Scopes Monkey Trial begins in Tennessee.

07-11.text: Aaron Burr shoots Alexander Hamilton in a duel.

07-12.text: Lincoln signs the law creating the Medal of Honor for the Army.

07-13.text: Live Aid concerts are held in London and Philadelphia.

07-14.text: Parisians storm the Bastille, starting the French Revolution.

07-15.text: French soldiers find the Rosetta Stone in Egypt (date as usually given).

07-16.text: The first atomic bomb is tested in New Mexico.

07-18.text: Nelson Mandela is born in South Africa.

07-19.text: The Seneca Falls Convention for women's rights opens.

07-20.text: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon: "The Eagle has landed."

07-21.text: The First Battle of Bull Run, the first major Civil War battle.

07-22.text: Wiley Post completes the first solo flight around the world.

07-23.text: Ford Motor Company sells its first car.

07-25.text: Louise Brown, the first test-tube baby, is born in England.

07-26.text: The agency that becomes the FBI is founded.

07-27.text: An armistice ends the fighting in the Korean War.

07-28.text: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia, starting World War I.

07-29.text: Eisenhower signs the law creating NASA.

07-31.text: The first US patent is issued, for a potash-making process.

08-01.text: MTV goes on the air with Video Killed the Radio Star.

08-02.text: Most delegates sign the engrossed Declaration of Independence.

08-03.text: Columbus sets sail from Palos, Spain.

08-04.text: The Coast Guard is born as the Revenue Cutter Service.

08-05.text: The first transatlantic telegraph cable is completed.

08-06.text: Gertrude Ederle becomes the first woman to swim the English Channel.

08-07.text: Washington creates the Badge of Military Merit, forerunner of the Purple Heart.

08-08.text: The Beatles are photographed walking across Abbey Road.

08-09.text: Nixon resigns and Gerald Ford becomes president.

08-11.text: Alcatraz opens as a federal prison.

08-13.text: East Germany begins building the Berlin Wall.

08-14.text: Japan agrees to surrender, ending World War II: V-J Day.

08-15.text: The Woodstock festival begins in New York State.

08-16.text: Gold is found in the Klondike, Yukon.

08-17.text: Robert Fulton's steamboat makes its first trip up the Hudson.

08-18.text: The 19th Amendment is ratified, giving US women the vote.

08-19.text: France gives the daguerreotype photo process to the world.

08-22.text: The yacht America wins the race that becomes the America's Cup.

08-23.text: Lunar Orbiter 1 takes the first photo of Earth from near the Moon.

08-24.text: Mount Vesuvius erupts and buries Pompeii (traditional date).

08-25.text: The National Park Service is created.

08-26.text: Krakatoa begins its massive eruption in Indonesia.

08-27.text: Edwin Drake strikes oil in Pennsylvania, launching the oil industry.

08-28.text: Martin Luther King Jr. gives his I Have a Dream speech.

08-30.text: The Moscow-Washington hotline goes into service.

08-31.text: Thomas Edison patents the Kinetograph movie camera.

09-01.text: Germany invades Poland, starting World War II in Europe.

09-02.text: Japan formally surrenders aboard the USS Missouri.

09-03.text: The Treaty of Paris is signed, ending the Revolutionary War.

09-04.text: George Eastman patents his Kodak roll-film camera.

09-05.text: The first Labor Day parade marches in New York City.

09-06.text: Magellan's ship Victoria completes the first voyage around the world.

09-07.text: The Blitz begins as Germany bombs London.

09-10.text: Elias Howe patents the sewing machine.

09-11.text: Alexander Hamilton becomes the first Treasury Secretary.

09-12.text: Teenagers discover the Lascaux cave paintings in France.

09-13.text: Congress sets the first US federal elections.

09-14.text: Francis Scott Key writes the Star-Spangled Banner.

09-15.text: Charles Darwin's HMS Beagle reaches the Galapagos.

09-16.text: The Mayflower sails from Plymouth, England.

09-17.text: The US Constitution is signed in Philadelphia.

09-18.text: George Washington lays the US Capitol's cornerstone.

09-19.text: New Zealand becomes the first country where women can vote.

09-20.text: Magellan sets sail from Spain to circle the globe.

09-21.text: J.R.R. Tolkien's The Hobbit is published.

09-22.text: Lincoln issues the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation.

09-23.text: Astronomers in Berlin find the planet Neptune.

09-24.text: The Judiciary Act creates the US Supreme Court's structure.

09-25.text: Congress sends the Bill of Rights to the states.

09-26.text: West Side Story opens on Broadway.

09-27.text: The world's first public steam railway opens in England.

09-29.text: London's Metropolitan Police make their first patrols.

09-30.text: The USS Nautilus, the first nuclear submarine, is commissioned.

10-02.text: Charles Schulz's Peanuts comic strip debuts.

10-04.text: The Soviets launch Sputnik, starting the Space Age.

10-05.text: The Beatles release their first single, Love Me Do.

10-06.text: The Jazz Singer, the first talking feature film, premieres.

10-07.text: Ford starts its moving assembly line.

10-09.text: The Washington Monument opens to the public.

10-10.text: The US Naval Academy opens in Annapolis.

10-11.text: Apollo 7, the first crewed Apollo flight, launches.

10-13.text: The White House cornerstone is laid.

10-14.text: Chuck Yeager breaks the sound barrier.

10-15.text: I Love Lucy premieres on CBS.

10-16.text: Walt and Roy Disney found the Disney company.

10-17.text: The British surrender at Saratoga, a turning point of the Revolution.

10-18.text: The US formally takes over Alaska from Russia.

10-20.text: General MacArthur returns to the Philippines: "I have returned."

10-21.text: Admiral Nelson wins the Battle of Trafalgar.

10-22.text: Andre-Jacques Garnerin makes the first parachute jump, over Paris.

10-23.text: Apple unveils the iPod: 1,000 songs in your pocket.

10-25.text: Henry V wins the Battle of Agincourt.

10-26.text: The Erie Canal opens, linking the Great Lakes to New York City.

10-27.text: New York City's first subway line opens.

10-28.text: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated.

10-29.text: Black Tuesday: the stock market crashes.

10-30.text: Orson Welles's War of the Worlds broadcast alarms listeners.

11-01.text: Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling is first shown to the public.

11-02.text: KDKA in Pittsburgh makes the first commercial radio broadcast.

11-03.text: Laika the dog orbits Earth aboard Sputnik 2.

11-04.text: Howard Carter finds the steps to King Tut's tomb.

11-05.text: The Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament is foiled.

11-07.text: The Bolsheviks seize power in Russia's October Revolution.

11-10.text: Stanley finds Livingstone: "Dr. Livingstone, I presume?"

11-11.text: The Armistice ends the fighting of World War I at 11 a.m.

11-12.text: Ellis Island closes after processing 12 million immigrants.

11-13.text: The Vietnam Veterans Memorial is dedicated.

11-14.text: Herman Melville's Moby-Dick is published in the US.

11-15.text: Congress adopts the Articles of Confederation.

11-16.text: The Sound of Music opens on Broadway.

11-18.text: US railroads adopt standard time zones.

11-21.text: The Pilgrims sign the Mayflower Compact.

11-22.text: President John F. Kennedy is assassinated in Dallas.

11-23.text: The first jukebox plays in a San Francisco saloon.

11-24.text: Darwin's On the Origin of Species is published.

11-25.text: Agatha Christie's The Mousetrap opens in London; it's still running.

11-26.text: The first national Thanksgiving, proclaimed by George Washington.

11-27.text: Alfred Nobel signs his will, creating the Nobel Prizes.

11-28.text: Magellan sails into the ocean he names the Pacific.

11-29.text: Richard Byrd's crew makes the first flight over the South Pole.

11-30.text: Winston Churchill is born at Blenheim Palace.

12-01.text: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat in Montgomery.

12-02.text: The first nuclear chain reaction is achieved in Chicago.

12-03.text: Christiaan Barnard performs the first human heart transplant.

12-04.text: Washington bids his officers farewell at Fraunces Tavern.

12-06.text: Edison records "Mary had a little lamb" on his phonograph.

12-08.text: Reagan and Gorbachev sign the INF nuclear arms treaty.

12-09.text: A Charlie Brown Christmas first airs.

12-10.text: The first Nobel Prizes are awarded.

12-12.text: Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal.

12-13.text: Francis Drake sets sail on his voyage around the world.

12-14.text: Roald Amundsen reaches the South Pole.

12-15.text: The Bill of Rights is ratified.

12-17.text: The Wright brothers make the first powered airplane flight.

12-18.text: The 13th Amendment abolishing slavery is proclaimed.

12-19.text: Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol is published.

12-20.text: The US formally takes over Louisiana in New Orleans.

12-21.text: Disney's Snow White premieres, the first full-length cel-animated film.

12-22.text: Edward Johnson lights the first electric Christmas tree.

12-23.text: Bell Labs demonstrates the first transistor.

12-24.text: Apollo 8 orbits the Moon and reads Genesis on Christmas Eve.

12-25.text: Washington crosses the icy Delaware River.

12-26.text: Marie and Pierre Curie announce the discovery of radium.

12-27.text: Radio City Music Hall opens in New York.

12-28.text: The Lumiere brothers hold the first public movie screening, in Paris.

12-31.text: Edison shows off his electric light at Menlo Park.
